resources.string: Runs your scripts when the IDE opens or closes a project, opens, saves or closes a file, or builds. Off until you turn it on.
Name an executable script after a hook, or put several in <hook>.d/. Scripts in actions/ appear as Run <name> on a file\'s menu. In the Terminal this folder is ~/.config/codeonthego/hooks.

resources.string: Stop a script after this many seconds
Enter a whole number of seconds from %1$d to %2$d. The timeout stays at %3$d until you do.

Scripts in a project\'s .codeonthego/hooks folder run only after you read and trust them in the Hooks tab, because a script can arrive with a project: a cloned repository, or an AI agent\'s edit. They need no executable bit.

plurals.name: hk_review_hidden
plurals.item: %1$d character is shown as <U+XXXX>, highlighted: a character outside plain ASCII, a carriage return, or a space or tab at the end of a line. Any of these can make a script run differently from how it reads; after a backslash, a hidden one turns what looks like a line continuation into a separate command. Do not trust the script unless you know why it is there.
